The Wuhan Corona Virus Outbreak

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An outbreak of a novel Coronavirus has the world terrified. What will happen when it reaches South Africa and how will we cope?

Unique Selling Point:
As the corona virus spreads to a number of countries around the world, we investigate whether South Africa is really prepared for this looming epidemic…

Summary:
The 21st century has seen the emergence of several new and deadly diseases such as SARS, Ebola & Swine Flu. The latest surfaced in the Chinese city of Wuhan at the end of 2019. Since then, this novel coronavirus has infected over 17000 people, mostly in China but has now also spread to several countries around the world.

Similar to SARS, this new virus causes pneumonia and has already resulted in 362 deaths.

We speak to South Africans living in Wuhan about their experience of living in a city that is the epicentre of a potential pandemic.

Currently there are no reported cases in South Africa but with infections reported in over 26 countries (other than China) it may only be a matter of time before the virus reaches local shores.

We investigate whether how South Africa is preparing to deal with a looming epidemic

Press Release:


Corona Virus: Testing South Africa’s Readiness
The Corona Virus, which has been declared a Global Health emergency, has countries on high alert as international scientists scramble to find a cure. As the number of confirmed cases of the various continues to rise worldwide and hundreds already dead, we investigate whether South Africa is really prepared for this potential epidemic.
Producer: Julian Sun | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


SCRIPT
V/O: It began on the 31st of December in the Chinese city of Wuhan.

“China’s health commission is warning the ability of the deadly corona virus to spread is getting stronger…”

V/O: A new virus never seen before… spreading rapidly

People in Wuhan have been asked not to leave the city and outsiders have been told to stay away

V/O: An entire city quarantined, a world on high alert

There is literally no treatment or vaccine available at the moment

V/O: Spreading to other parts of the globe in just a few short weeks

The virus is on the move and that’s what makes it so scary

Canada, US, France, Australia and Thailand among those treating patients with the virus

V/O: Causing the World Health Organization to declare the coronavirus a global emergency

We’re basically at a pandemic now.

MASA LINK: Since the
virus first emerged in December, there have been thousands of cases reported and hundreds of deaths. With no cure currently available, that number is sure to climb. The biggest concern is how high it will go.

V/O: Professor Cheryl Cohen from the National Institute of Communicable Disease explains the origin of the virus

o Food Market in Wuhan
o From Corona Virus family
o Crossed over from animals to humans

V/O: Professor Adriano Duse from Wits Medical School is an expert on the pathogens that cause infectious diseases.

o What is a corona virus?
o How it makes people sick – causes pneumomia
o Who it’s affecting the most – elderly and sickly
o Mortality rate, infection rate

V/O: Since the start of the year, the virus (dubbed 2019-nCoV) has spread rapidly. From just a handful of cases at the beginning of January, there are now over 30 000 infections confirmed.

The majority of these are in Mainland China but it has also been detected in 27 other countries.

V/O: Wuhan is home to over 11 million people, including hundreds of South Africans. On January 23rd, it was placed under quarantine, with air & rail traffic suspended.

Sibusiso Sgwane was able to escape on one of the last flights out.

o Took one of the last flights out to Vietnam
o What it was like in the city before he left

V/O: Roxanne Rawlins wasn’t able to leave. For the past few weeks she’s been living in a city in lockdown.

o What it’s been like to live in Wuhan
o Empty streets
o Empty Shops

V/O: With thousands of new cases reported each day, travel with China has been severely restricted or even banned, as authorities try desperately to contain the spread of the virus.

o -Prof Duse on the economic impact of the virus re air travel and the fear it spreads

With the world on high alert, what is South Africa’s plan? Minister of Health Zweli Mkhize explains how the country is preparing to deal with the virus.

o Can you confirm that there are no confirmed cases in South Africa?
o How is South Africa preparing
o The NICD as the spearhead of South Africa’s response


o Cheryl Cohen on NICD plans, operations centre
o Ports of entry


V/O: This is a national effort that will see the Department of Health & The NICD coordinating with both government-run & private hospitals

Dr Anchen Laubscher is the Medical Director of the Netcare Group

o Anchen Laubscher on Netcare’s preparedness and working with the Department of Health
o Intercut with Cheryl & Zweli
o 3 government hospitals earmarked to handle cases
o Same protocol sent to all health services, public & private


o Walk us through a scenario: a patient comes to the hospital complaining of flu-like symptoms, shortness of breath… They were in China 2 weeks ago.
o Patient isolated, tested and then moved to isolation ward.
o Protecting healthcare professionals

V/O:As the virus continues to spread, is it only a matter of time before it reaches South Africa?

o Is it inevitable?


V/O: Currently there is no vaccine for 2019-nCoV. So how worried should we be?

o Comments about how seriously we should take this
o And what they think will happen

V/O: Fortunately there have been no confirmed cases in the country. Right now the only South Africans at risk are a world away, trapped in the stricken city of Wuhan

o Video Diary of Roxanne walking the empty streets of Wuhan
o Her message to her family that she’s safe.
